lead: I'm interested in how societies keep the lights on and the homes warm while moving to cleaner, fairer energy systems.
body:
## Hello, I'm Oladayo

I'm a graduate student in the **Master of Sustainability** programme at the **University of Saskatchewan**, specialising in **Energy Security**. I started this site at the beginning of the programme because I learn best when I have to explain things and because the questions I care about are better answered in conversation than alone.

## Academic background

BSc in Systems Engineering, University of Lagos.



## Professional background

I bring more than eight years of experience across oil and gas and banking, including work as a project execution engineer on oil-and-gas projects in Nigeria. My background has developed a practical interest in project delivery, risk, affordability, financing, and the conditions that shape whether energy solutions can be implemented responsibly. My current learning focuses on affordable and clean energy, renewable energy, community energy planning, and the relationships between technical performance, equity, governance, and local knowledge. I am particularly interested in decentralized solar–hydrogen hubs and the potential to repurpose decommissioned oil-and-gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta.

## Why sustainability and energy security?

Energy sits underneath almost everything - health, livelihoods, education, industry, and the way communities plan for the future. Yet the systems we rely on are being asked to change faster than at any point in living memory. I wanted to understand that change properly: not just the technologies, but the policies, institutions and people that decide whether a transition is secure, affordable and fair.

My interest in sustainability grew from my experience in the oil and gas industry, where I saw firsthand the important role energy plays in economic development, as well as the environmental and social challenges associated with its production. This experience inspired me to explore how we can build energy systems that are reliable, affordable, equitable, and environmentally responsible.

## What I hope to do with this

After completing the programme, I hope to combine my energy-sector experience with advanced knowledge of sustainability, energy security, and data-informed decision-making. My goal is to contribute to practical energy-transition strategies, policies, and projects that improve energy reliability and affordability while advancing environmental responsibility and social equity. I am particularly interested in renewable energy, the repurposing of existing oil and gas infrastructure, and solutions that support resilient communities in emerging economies.

## A note on this site

The views here are my own and reflect my learning as it happens. Some posts will be rough or incomplete, and I'll update them as my thinking changes. Where I draw on other people's work, I try to credit it clearly.
